body:
Question stem:
Answer all parts of the following question.

(a) Sketch the cycle with arrows and label where temperature is greatest.

(b) Determine the net work done by the gas per cycle.

(c) Determine the net heat added per cycle and explain the sign using the first law.

Stimulus:
One mole of ideal gas follows a clockwise rectangular cycle on a P-V diagram: (V₀,P₀) to (V₀,3P₀) to (2V₀,3P₀) to (2V₀,P₀) and back.

Question stem:
Answer all parts of the following question.

(a) For the RC circuit as it charges, state the capacitor voltage, resistor voltage, and current at each of three times: t=0, t=τ (one time constant, τ=RC), and long after (t→∞). Then use Kirchhoff's loop rule to explain why V_R = ε − V_C holds at every instant during charging, not just at these three points.

(b) Give a quantitative energy accounting for the charging process: how much total energy does the battery deliver, how much ends up stored in the capacitor, and how much is dissipated as heat in the resistor? Then explain whether this energy split depends on the value of R.

Stimulus:
An initially uncharged capacitor charges through a resistor from an ideal battery. At t=RC it has reached about 63% of its final charge.

Question stem:
Determining a converging lens focal length: Answer all mandatory subparts. Show reasoning and calculations clearly. Use standard AP Physics notation and justify qualitative claims.

Stimulus:
A student has a converging lens of unknown focal length, an illuminated object, a movable screen, an optical bench with a meter scale, and a ruler. The student can obtain several sharply focused real images.

Question stem:
A ray strikes a plane mirror at 25° measured from the normal. Its reflection angle measured from the normal is

Choices:
A. 25°
B. 50°
C. 65°
D. 0°

Question stem:
Light enters glass from air at an oblique angle. Because glass has larger refractive index, the ray bends

Choices:
A. toward the normal
B. away from the normal
C. without changing direction
D. toward the surface

Question stem:
Answer all parts of the following question.

(a) Design a feasible measurement that tests the thin-lens equation; identify the independent variable, dependent variable, and one control.

(b) Explain why assuming the lens thickness is negligible compared to the object and image distances justifies applying the thin-lens equation directly rather than a thick-lens model.

Stimulus:
A converging lens is available for designing a measurement of the thin-lens equation.

Question stem:
The magnetic flux into the page through a loop is increasing. The induced current is

Choices:
A. clockwise
B. counterclockwise
C. zero
D. depends on the loop's resistance

Question stem:
Answer all parts of the following question.

(a) Represent the changes in electric potential energy and kinetic energy with an energy bar chart.

(b) Calculate the proton's kinetic energy in electron-volts and joules.

(c) Determine its speed, and describe how the answers change for an electron released from rest at 200 V and accelerated toward 800 V.

Stimulus:
A proton starts from rest at electric potential 800 V and moves to a region at 200 V. Neglect gravity.

Question stem:
Answer all parts of the following question.

(a) Predict how capacitance, voltage, electric field, and stored energy change.

(b) Explain which predictions would differ if the battery remained connected.

Stimulus:
A charged parallel-plate capacitor is disconnected from its battery. Its plate separation is then doubled while charge remains fixed.

Question stem:
A particle with charge q moves with speed v in a direction parallel to a uniform magnetic field of magnitude B. The magnetic force on the particle is--

Choices:
A. qvB
B. qvB, directed parallel to v
C. zero
D. qvB, directed perpendicular to both v and B

Question stem:
Answer all parts of the following question.

(a) Derive the image distance and magnification produced by the lens, and evaluate their numeric values.

(b) Explain how the thin-lens equation follows from treating the lens as infinitely thin with paraxial (small-angle) rays, and how the sign convention gives a negative magnification for a real inverted image.

Stimulus:
A converging lens has focal length 0.200 m and an object is 0.600 m from the lens.

Question stem:
A long straight wire carries current upward. At a point directly east of the wire, the magnetic field points

Choices:
A. north
B. south
C. east
D. west

Question stem:
A charged particle moves perpendicular to uniform B. If its speed doubles with q, m, and B fixed, its circular-path radius

Choices:
A. halves
B. stays the same
C. doubles
D. quadruples

Question stem:
Answer all parts of the following question.

(a) Derive the capacitor's time constant and its voltage as a function of time while charging, and evaluate the numeric expression.

(b) Explain how Kirchhoff's voltage law applied to the RC loop yields the exponential charging equation, and how assuming an ideal battery with no internal resistance and an initially uncharged capacitor justifies the given initial condition.

Stimulus:
An initially uncharged 20.0 μF capacitor charges through 100 kΩ from a 12.0 V battery.

Question stem:
Answer all parts of the following question.

(a) Predict how the heat added changes when the temperature change is doubled, and justify the prediction quantitatively.

(b) Explain, without repeating the specific numbers from part (a), why Q is directly proportional to ΔT in this process at all -- referencing the facts that internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature and that constant volume means no boundary work is done.

Stimulus:
One mole of an ideal monatomic gas is heated at constant volume from 300 K to 360 K.

Question stem:
A plane mirror forms an image that is

Choices:
A. real and inverted
B. virtual and upright
C. real and enlarged
D. virtual and inverted

Question stem:
Answer all parts of the following question.

(a) Translate the first-law relation for this constant-volume process into a labeled P-V diagram, and explain what the (zero) enclosed area indicates about the work done.

(b) Explain why the work done by the gas is zero at constant volume and how the monatomic ideal-gas assumption fixes the value of Cv used to compute ΔU.

Stimulus:
One mole of an ideal monatomic gas is heated at constant volume from 300 K to 360 K.

Question stem:
Under what condition can total internal reflection occur?

Choices:
A. Light travels from a lower-index to a higher-index medium
B. Light travels from a higher-index to a lower-index medium at an angle of incidence above the critical angle
C. Light strikes the boundary at normal incidence (0 degrees)
D. Light travels through a vacuum

Question stem:
A converging lens forms a real inverted image when the object is

Choices:
A. inside the focal length
B. at the focal point
C. beyond the focal length
D. at infinity only

Question stem:
Charging a capacitor through two resistors: Answer all mandatory subparts. Show reasoning and calculations clearly. Use standard AP Physics notation and justify qualitative claims.

Stimulus:
An initially uncharged capacitor C is connected in series with resistors R and 2R and an ideal battery of emf ε. At t=0 an ideal switch is closed. Calculus is not required; you may use the standard charging form q(t)=Q_f(1-e^{-t/τ}).

Question stem:
Answer all parts of the following question.

(a) Describe a procedure to determine focal length using several object positions.

(b) State a graph whose slope/intercept can be used and one uncertainty precaution.

Stimulus:
An unknown converging lens, illuminated object, screen, and meterstick are available.

Question stem:
Answer all parts of the following question.

(a) Derive the magnitude of the magnetic force on the ion and describe the path it follows, and evaluate the force expression.

(b) Explain how Newton's second law leads to circular motion for this ion, identifying which force provides the centripetal force, and state why the assumption that velocity is exactly perpendicular to B is needed for the force expression used in part (a) to apply.

Stimulus:
A singly charged positive ion moves at 3.00×10⁵ m/s perpendicular to a uniform 0.200 T magnetic field.

Question stem:
Lenz's law determines the induced current's

Choices:
A. magnitude only
B. direction
C. resistance
D. charge carrier mass

Question stem:
Answer all parts of the following question.

(a) Draw and label the principal axis, mirror, F, C, object, and image. Use any two valid principal rays to locate the image and show the arrow directions.

(b) State the image's orientation, relative size, and whether it is real or virtual.

Stimulus:
An upright object is placed on the principal axis between the focal point F and center of curvature C of an ideal spherical concave mirror. Use the paraxial-ray approximation.
